headline: Growth holds, but cash flow and guidance both slip
summary_short: HCA Healthcare grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 8.7% y/y to $20.230 billion and diluted EPS 11.6% to $7.62, but operating cash flow fell 44.5% y/y to $2.335 billion as a one-time Florida Medicaid payment-program catch-up inflated both revenue and expense, and full-year net income, EBITDA and EPS guidance were trimmed.
summary_long: Revenue rose 8.7% y/y to $20.23B and diluted EPS rose 11.6% to $7.62 as Adjusted EBITDA grew 4.6% to $4.027B. A roughly $400M payer-mix hit from ACA exchange coverage losses was offset by a $400M Medicaid Supplemental Payment Programs benefit, mainly a Florida directed-payment catch-up (recognizing $1.372B revenue and $829M expense this quarter, much of it for pre-2026 periods) — which inflated both lines without matching cash, driving operating cash flow down 44.5% y/y to $2.335B. Cash was $1.013B against $49.7B debt; the company repurchased $2.064B of stock and paid a $0.78/share dividend. Full-year net income, EBITDA and EPS guidance were each trimmed from January's ranges; capex guidance of $5.0-5.5B held unchanged.

drivers.explanation: Same-facility admissions rose 2.5% and revenue per equivalent admission rose 6.4%, plus one-time recognition of $1.372B in Florida directed-payment-program revenue covering periods back to October 2024.

Growth was tempered by a roughly $400M unfavorable payer-mix impact from ACA exchange coverage losses, partly offset by a roughly $400M incremental Medicaid Supplemental Payment Programs benefit and $10M of facility-sale gains.
EPS grew faster than net income partly because the diluted share count fell to 222.8M from 241.9M a year ago after continued buybacks, on top of the net income drivers above.
Reflects the same payer-mix headwind and Medicaid Supplemental Payment Programs benefit affecting net income, netted against underlying volume and expense growth.
H1 operating cash flow fell as accounts receivable built $1.417B (versus a $320M source of cash a year ago), consistent with Florida DPP revenue recognized this quarter not yet collected in cash.

Full-year 2026 guidance for net income, Adjusted EBITDA and diluted EPS was each lowered from January's initial ranges; revenue guidance was narrowed to $77.0-$79.5B and capex guidance of $5.0-5.5B held unchanged.
